newsitem.title: CROATIA: Kras steals limelight as Croatian shares end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Kras steals limelight as Croatian shares end mixed.

text.p: Chocolate-maker Kras stole the spotlight among Croatian stocks on Wednesday, as trade returned to its routine after soaring on Tuesday and prices ended mixed.
Traders predicted no big shake-ups would hit the market in the near future. "I don't expect any big changes in the next week or two," said Igor Kos of the Taurus brokerage.
Six of 17 active issues rose on Wednesday, six fell and five were flat. The volume halved to 7,791 units and turnover was down to 6.5 million kuna from Tuesday's 25.4 million.
Croatia's leading chocolate maker Kras added 18 kuna or 4.3 percent to 420 on volume of 1,792 shares, following the news that its net profit in 1996 rose 25 percent.
"Kras is still oscillating within its routine limits. It's an interesting stock and will certainly break through, but not very soon," Kos said.
Ratko Bubalo of Eastbrokers said prices of Kras and food processor Podravka were under pressure as small shareholders, who were running short of cash, were profit-taking.
"But based on its good results for 1996, Kras finally began is way up and this is going to continue," Bubalo said. Podravka lost seven kuna to 283 on volume of 1,400 shares.
The market heavyweights, fully-listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, continued to slide in line with the decrease of their Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in London.
Pliva lost 7.5 kuna to 452.5, nearing its resistance point, which the traders put at 450 kuna, on volume of 384 units.

Zagrebacka was the day's most active issue, inching down 21 kuna to 2,000 on volume of 2,063 units. But both its 2C and 3E series were gainers, adding five kuna to 815 and 10 kuna to 1,160, respectively.
"Zagrebacka 3-E series is one of the top shares now, with lots of space for further growth," Bubalo said.
Kos said both Pliva's and Zagrebacka's prices would undergo slight corrections.
"We are worried by the decline in Pliva's sales which could drag its price down a bit in the future," echoed Bubalo.
Wednesday's biggest gainer was textile firm Varteks, adding 10 kuna or 14.3 percent to 80 kuna, on volume of 470 units. Varteks recently renewed its contract with Levi Strauss & Co.

Hotelier Istraturist led the decliners. It lost 8 kuna or 4 percent to 185 on volume of 100 shares. Of four other hotelier stocks two were flat, one fell and Riviera Porec was the only gainer, up 13 kuna to 160 on volume of 428 shares.
